claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems can be used to produce a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Replacing conventional alloys with compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems is the proposed intervention.
The proposed behavior occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Alloy composition is the structural mediator linking the intervention to the behavior.
Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems resist temper embrittlement.
The predicted outcome is a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Conventional alloys exhibit temper embrittlement and serve as the baseline.
The relevant boundary is the temperature range in which temper embrittlement occurs.

contradictions.description: Temper-embrittlement resistance would suppress the intermediate brittle regime rather than explain a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.

The hypothesis proposes the alloy systems for a ductile–brittle–ductile transition, while the stated mechanism is resistance to temper embrittlement and the experiment treats observation of temper embrittlement as falsifying. Thus the proposed source of the brittle interval is internally unclear.
